ai.description: This frog reaches 4–5 cm. It is olive-brown with dark spots, a pale belly, and a distinct, pungent odor. It features a pointed snout and expanded toe discs adapted for fast-flowing mountain streams.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Amolops nidorbellus* is best distinguished by the prominent, distinct dark spots scattered across its dorsal surface, which are absent in most other similar *Amolops* species.
ai.habitat: *Amolops nidorbellus* inhabits fast-flowing, rocky streams within subtropical evergreen forests in the Northeast Indian hills, typically at elevations between 600–1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Spotted Stinky Torrent Frog is primarily nocturnal and emits a pungent, garlic-like odor from its skin glands when threatened to deter potential predators.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Amolops nidorbellus* breeds during the monsoon season, laying eggs in aquatic environments. Specific clutch sizes remain undocumented in current scientific literature.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Amolops nidorbellus* is endemic to the Mishmi Hills in Arunachal Pradesh, India, where it inhabits high-altitude torrents within the Eastern Himalayas.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Amolops nidorbellus* consists of a series of short, high-pitched, whistled notes emitted by males residing near fast-flowing mountain torrents.
